extracted.intended_audience: Recipients and subrecipients of Federal awards (grantees), pass-through entities, cognizant agencies; includes IHEs, nonprofits, and state/local governments
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and rules from 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart E describing which costs are allowable or unallowable under Federal awards, allocation and accounting requirements, and special rules for specific cost categories (e.g., fringe benefits, depreciation, litigation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable leave costs (accrual basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient or subrecipient uses the accrual basis of accounting, allowable leave costs are the lesser of the amount accrued or funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when leave is earned; recipient must charge the lesser of accrued amount or funded amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of fringe benefits (employer contributions or expenses for social security; employee life, health, unemployment, and worker's compensation insurance; pension plan costs; and other similar benefits) are allowable provided such benefits are permitted under established written policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fringe benefits must be allocated to Federal awards and other activities consistent with the pattern of benefits attributable to the employees whose salaries/wages are charged, and charged as direct or indirect costs following the recipient's accounting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits — assignment to cost objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient or subrecipient may assign fringe benefits to cost objectives by identifying specific benefits to specific employees or by allocating them based on entity‑wide salaries and wages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using allocation, separate allocations must be made to selective groupings of employees unless recipient demonstrates costs in relationship to salaries/wages do not differ significantly among groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance costs (self-insurance and claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions for reserves under a self-insurance program for unemployment or workers' compensation are allowable to the extent they represent reasonable estimates of liabilities; insurance costs on lives of officers/employees allowable only to the extent they represent additional compensation; actual claims paid are allowable in year of payment if consistent costing policy is followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions for self-insured liabilities not payable for more than one year must not exceed present value; insurance costs where recipient is beneficiary are unallowable; see §§200.447(d)(1) and (2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automobile personal use
rubrics_metrics.description: Portion of automobile costs relating to personal use by employees (including transportation to/from work) is unallowable as a fringe benefit or indirect cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable regardless of whether the cost is reported as taxable income to employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pension plan costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Pension plan costs incurred in accordance with established written policies are allowable provided policies are reasonable, allocation methods non-discriminatory, and costs are determined in accordance with GAAP (except State/local governments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional rules: costs should be funded for all participants within six months after fiscal year end (with limits on increases caused by delayed funding beyond 30 days after each quarter), premiums for ERISA termination insurance allowable (late payment charges and certain excise taxes unallowable), pension costs may be computed pay-as-you-go or actuarial GAAP methods, pay-as-you-go limited to actual payments, actuarial method allowable if funded within six months (or as agreed), excess funded amounts may be used in future periods, unfunded liability at conversion allowable if amortized per GAAP, unfunded pension costs cannot be charged directly to a Federal award if not allocable, and Federal Government must receive equitable share of any previously allowed pension costs that revert or inure to recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-retirement health plan (PRHP) costs
rubrics_metrics.description: PRHP costs (health insurance/services for retirees and beneficiaries not included in pension plan) may be computed using pay-as-you-go or actuarial cost methods recognized by GAAP and consistent with written policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay-as-you-go limited to actual payments; actuarial costs allowable if funded within six months after fiscal year end (or later if cognizant agency agrees); excess funded amounts may be used in future periods; initial unfunded liability on conversion may be amortized per GAAP or negotiated period; unfunded PRHP costs cannot be charged directly to Federal awards if not allocable; to be allowable in current year, PRHP costs must be paid to an insurer/provider as current year costs or to a trustee maintaining a trust/reserve solely for post-retirement benefits; recipient must provide Federal Government equitable share of any previously allowed PRHP costs that revert or inure to recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severance pay allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Severance (dismissal wages) is allowable only to the extent required by law, employer-employee agreement, established policy (implied agreement), or circumstances of particular employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs divided: (i) actual severance for normal turnover allocated to all activities or charged to a reasonable reserve; (ii) accruals for abnormal/mass severance are not allowable (prior approval required for Federal share of specific payments); severance pay in excess of standard severance contingent on change in control is unallowable; severance payments to foreign nationals outside U.S. subject to limitations (unallowable if exceed customary U.S. practices unless required by foreign law or necessary for performance and approved); severance due to closing/curtailment abroad unallowable unless required by foreign law or necessary and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHE tuition and remission fringe benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: For institutions of higher education: undergraduate/graduate tuition or tuition remission for employees is allowable if granted under established written policies and distributed equitably; tuition benefits for family members are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tuition remission for non-employee individuals limited to tax-free amount under IRC 26 U.S.C. 127; waivers/reductions ok if not discriminatory in favor of highly compensated employees; employees may exercise benefits at other institutions per policy; see §200.466 for treatment of tuition remission to students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefit programs for state/local funded IHEs
rubrics_metrics.description: For IHEs whose costs are paid by State/local government, fringe benefit programs (pension, FICA) and other benefit costs incurred specifically for the IHE are allowable subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: costs must meet Basic Considerations (§§200.402–200.411), be supported by approved cost allocation plans per Federal cost accounting principles, and not be otherwise borne directly/indirectly by the Federal Government; allowability doesn't depend on whether recorded in IHE accounting records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference costs allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: A conference is an event whose primary purpose is to disseminate technical information beyond the recipient/subrecipient and is necessary and reasonable for successful performance under the Federal award. Allowable conference costs may include rental of facilities, speakers' fees, attendance fees, meals/refreshments, local transportation, and incidental items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs of identifying/providing locally available dependent-care resources allowable as needed; conference hosts must exercise discretion to ensure costs are appropriate, necessary, and minimized; Federal agency may authorize exceptions for Indian Tribes, children, and the elderly; see §§200.438, 200.456, and 200.475 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency provisions in budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Contingency provisions are budget estimates for future costs associated with possible events or conditions with indeterminable precise outcomes; contingency amounts for major project scope changes, unforeseen risks, or extraordinary events must not be included in Federal award budget estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other contingency amounts may be explicitly included to improve precision if estimated using broadly-accepted cost estimating methodologies specified in budget documentation and accepted by the Federal agency; to be allowable, actual costs must comply with cost principles (§§200.300 and 200.403), be necessary and reasonable, and verifiable from records. Payments to a contingency reserve or similar payment for unforeseen events are unallowable except as noted in §§200.431 and 200.447.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions and donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of contributions and donations (cash, property, services) from the recipient/subrecipient to other entities are unallowable; value of in-kind donations to recipient may not be charged to Federal award but may be used to meet cost sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depreciation on donated assets permitted provided donated property is not counted toward cost sharing; donated services value may not be charged but may meet cost sharing per §200.306; donated services/support should be supported by same methods as personnel allocability; nonprofit-specific rules: when donated services are material and supported by a significant amount of indirect costs, the value must be considered in determining indirect cost rate and allocated a proportionate share; where no basis for fair market value, recipient and cognizant agency must negotiate allocation; donated personal property and use of space value may not be charged to award but may be used to meet cost sharing and must be valued per §200.300; if treated as indirect costs, indirect cost rates must separate donation value so reimbursement is not made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense and prosecution costs (criminal/civil/administrative proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred in connection with criminal, civil, or administrative proceedings are not allowable if the proceeding relates to a violation or failure to comply with law/regulation/award terms by recipient (including agents/employees) and results in specified adverse dispositions (conviction, determination of liability, disallowance, debarment/suspension/award rescission/termination, or consent/compromise that could have resulted in such dispositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple proceedings involve same alleged misconduct, costs of all such proceedings are unallowable if any results in the described dispositions. Exceptions/allowability: (a) if Federal-initiated proceeding is resolved by consent/compromise and agreement expressly authorizes costs, they may be allowed; (b) if State/local/foreign proceeding, costs may be allowed if an authorized Federal official determines they were incurred as a result of a specific term/condition of the award or written direction of an authorized Federal official. In general, otherwise-allowable costs connected to proceedings may be allowed if reasonable/necessary/allocable, not prohibited by award, not recovered elsewhere, and an authorized Federal official determines a percentage allowed (generally ≤80% unless agreement provides otherwise). Costs potentially unallowable must be segregated and may be withheld pending resolution; conditional payment may be provided with adequate security. Additional rules: costs under Major Fraud Act (18 U.S.C. 1031) where recipient found liable or settled are unallowable; costs for prosecuting claims against the Federal Government (including appeals) are unallowable; patent infringement litigation costs are unallowable unless otherwise provided in the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation and capital asset costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Depreciation is the method for allocating the cost of fixed assets to periods benefitting from asset use. Recipients may be compensated for use of buildings, capital improvements, equipment, and capitalized software in accordance with GAAP, provided assets are needed and used and correctly allocated to Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation must follow Appendices III–IX. Depreciation computed on acquisition cost (donated asset uses fair market value at donation as acquisition cost). Acquisition cost excludes land, Federal-contributed portions, amounts already claimed as cost sharing, and assets acquired solely for non-Federal awards. Useful life must consider construction type, equipment nature, technology changes, historical data, and renewal/replacement policies. Depreciation method must reflect pattern of consumption; straight-line presumed appropriate absent evidence otherwise. Methods may not be changed without cognizant agency approval and must match financial statements. Buildings may be treated as single asset or componentized into building shell, building services systems, and fixed equipment; same method for indirect and financial statements required if componentizing. No depreciation allowed on assets outlived; when replacing use allowance, depreciation computed as if asset depreciated over entire life; total use allowance plus depreciation may not exceed acquisition cost. Adequate property records and inventories (at least every two years; sampling allowed) must support depreciation charges; maintain depreciation records showing amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee health and welfare costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred under established written policies for improving working conditions, employer-employee relations, employee health, and performance are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These costs must be equitably apportioned to all activities; income generated credited to costs unless irrevocably sent to employee welfare organizations. Losses from operating food services allowable only if objective is to operate on break-even basis, or if unusual circumstances are demonstrated and approved by the cognizant agency for indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment and prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Entertainment costs (amusement, diversion, social activities, gifts) are unallowable unless they have a specific and direct programmatic purpose and are included in a Federal award. Prizes or challenges are allowable if they have a specific and direct programmatic purpose and are included in the Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies should refer to OMB guidance M-10-11 (Guidance on the Use of Challenges and Prizes to Promote Open Government) or successor for prize/challenge guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and other capital expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules of allowability for capital expenditures: general purpose equipment, buildings, and land are allowable as direct costs only with prior written approval; special purpose equipment allowable as direct costs (items ≥ $10,000 require prior written approval); improvements that materially increase value/useful life allowable only with prior written approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When approved as direct costs, capital expenditures must be charged in the period incurred or as negotiated. Recipient may claim unamortized portion of equipment written off by continuing depreciation or amortizing amount over years negotiated with cognizant agency. Costs of disposal/transfer are allowable if Federal agency instructs. Equipment and other capital expenditures are unallowable as indirect costs. See §200.1 for definitions and §200.436/§200.465 for related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange rate fluctuation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost increases from fluctuations in exchange rates are allowable subject to availability of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior approval required only when change results in need for additional Federal funding or significantly reduces project scope; Federal agency must ensure adequate funds to avoid Antideficiency Act violation. Recipients must review local currency gains to determine need for additional funding before award expiration. Subsequent adjustments for currency increases may be allowable only with adequate source documentation from a commonly used source at time expense was made, and only to extent sufficient Federal funds are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fines, penalties, damages and settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs resulting from recipient/subrecipient violations of laws/regulations are unallowable, except when incurred as a result of compliance with specific provisions of the Federal award, or with prior written approval of the Federal agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §200.435 for related provisions on legal proceedings and allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising and investment management costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of organized fundraising (financial campaigns, endowment drives, solicitation of gifts/bequests) are unallowable. Fundraising costs for meeting Federal program objectives are allowable with prior written approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs of investment counsel/staff to enhance income from investments are unallowable except when associated with investments covering pension, self-insurance, or other funds with Federal participation allowed by this part. Costs related to physical custody/control of monies and securities are allowable. Both allowable and unallowable fundraising/investment activities must be allocated appropriate share of indirect costs per §200.413.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gains and losses on disposition of depreciable assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Gains and losses on sale, retirement, or other disposition of depreciable property must be included in year they occur as credits or charges to the asset cost grouping(s); amount equals proceeds minus undepreciated basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gains/losses must not be recognized separately under certain conditions (processed through depreciation account, exchange as part of purchase price of similar item, loss from failing to maintain proper insurance except as provided in §200.447, compensation provided through use allowances). Extraordinary or bulk sales retirements are case-by-case. Gains/losses from sale/exchange of property other than depreciable property excluded from Federal award costs. Disposal of assets acquired with Federal funds must follow §§200.310–200.316.

rubrics_metrics.name: General costs of government (state/local/tribal)
rubrics_metrics.description: For states, local governments, and Indian Tribes, general costs of government are unallowable except as provided in §200.475.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable costs include salaries/expenses of governor/chief executive, salaries/expenses of state legislature/tribal council/similar bodies, judicial branch costs, and costs of prosecutorial activities unless treated as a direct cost to a specific program if authorized by statute or regulation.
